prompt: Implement the classic turnstile state machine: a coin unlocks it, a push relocks it, and pushing while locked is blocked and counted -- state() reports "locked" or "unlocked".
explanation: A state machine pairs a current state with transition rules, and the whole thing fits in one boolean here: coin() moves the machine to unlocked no matter where it was (which silently absorbs the extra-coin case), while push() branches -- unlocked relocks, locked records a blocked attempt. Keeping the fields private and exposing only state() and blockedCount() means callers can drive the machine but never put it into an inconsistent state. This coin/push turnstile is the textbook introductory example of the State pattern; with more states you would graduate to an enum or state objects.
hints: Two fields suffice: a boolean (start it at locked = true) and an int counter.
coin() can simply set locked = false -- if it was already unlocked nothing visibly changes.
push() needs the if: locked ? increment the counter : set locked = true. state() just maps the boolean to "locked"/"unlocked".
